title: Prefix + Verb Together: The Neutral Word Order

sections.title: One tight, glued unit
sections.content: You already know from Unit 10 (*fel*, *hozzá*) that a prefix can stand apart from its verb; here is the whole pattern. Every prefixed verb from this whole unit — *bemegy*, *felkel*, *elkezd*, *megeszik*, and all the rest — keeps its *igekötő* (verb prefix) stuck directly onto the front of the verb in a plain, neutral sentence. Statements, and most questions too: the prefix and the verb move together as one glued unit, and nothing else is allowed to squeeze between them.

items.english: Károly sits down on the chair.
Anna gets out of the car.

sections.content: This glued order is the everyday default — reach for it in statements and in yes/no questions alike (*Bemész a boltba?* keeps be- glued too). There's one major exception, and it comes up constantly: negation.
